chunks: My father, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan all narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from ‘Ali ibn Ismā‘īl ibn ‘Īsā, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd al-Zayyāt, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh and Abā al-Ḥasan, and they both said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn on the Day of ‘Arafah, Allāh will turn him back with a heart filled with certainty.

key_terms.ثَلِجَ الْفُؤَادِ: With a heart filled with certainty/clarity
key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the unique spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine on the Day of ‘Arafah, linking the pilgrimage to the pivotal moment of divine covenant. The phrase 'thalj al-fu’ād' (snowy/cool heart) signifies the removal of spiritual heat and anxiety, granting the visitor profound tranquility and firm conviction. This reward underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt and the continuity of divine mercy through their designated times of worship.
